title: Skills hypotheses and experiments - personal backlog
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to convert fuzzy growth ideas into small experiments I can run in the next 3 months. Focus area: skill fluency for ICs and manager coaching quality for calibration/promotion readiness. NOT a final plan — a running notebook for things to try, evidence, and manager prep.

Top-level hypotheses (short):
- H1: Small, frequent micro-feedback cycles (2–3 min prompts right after work) will increase perceived coaching quality and clarity on next steps vs. monthly 1:1s.
- H2: Adding a lightweight rubric (3 signal categories) to interview debriefs will reduce inter-rater variance in candidate calibration by ~15% within two cycles.
- H3: Targeted paired calibration sessions (one people-ops + one eng manager) focusing on 5 edge-case promotions will surface 2 actionable changes to leveling guidance.

How I'll test each (experiments):
- Experiment A: Micro-feedback pilot
  - Who: two small IC pods (8–12 people total) + 4 managers
  - What: after each ship/demo, send a one-question pulse: "What went well / one concrete next step?" via Slack thread (template below)
  - Duration: 6 weeks
  - Signal to measure: participation rate, % of responses that include a concrete next step, manager follow-up actions recorded in 1:1 notes
  - Success criteria: 40%+ response rate and at least 25% of responses with actionable next steps recorded

- Experiment B: 3-point rubric for debriefs
  - Rubric draft: Technical breadth (0–2), Impact & scope (0–2), Growth signal (0–2); comments required for any score of 0 or 2
  - Who: apply to next 12 candidate debriefs across platform and infra hiring
  - Measure: variance in scores across reviewers, duration of debrief, hiring committee confidence (survey)
  - Success criteria: reduce standard deviation by 15% and retain hiring velocity (no >10% extra time per debrief)

- Experiment C: Paired calibration sessions
  - Format: 1.5 hour working session, one case study per session, capture suggested changes inline
  - Who: volunteer eng managers (3) + people-ops (me) for 3 sessions
  - output: one doc per session with 2–3 suggested changes and sample language for leveling guidance
  - Success criteria: at least 2 suggestions accepted into the skills framework draft

Quick manager prep (for upcoming 1:1):
- Agenda I want:
  1) Quick status: micro-feedback pilot ask and permission to run pilot in two pods
  2) Ask for a champion manager (name(s) prep: Priya, Marco) and time commitment
  3) Preview rubric for debriefs and ask for a short trial in upcoming interviews
  4) Seek support to run paired calibration and identify 3 candidate promotion edge cases
- Evidence to bring: short slide with pilot design (1 slide), expected manager time investment per week (5–10 mins), sample Slack template, sample rubric
- Framing language: "Low-risk experiment to surface clearer next steps for ICs and reduce wash on debriefs. I’m asking for permission to run for 6 weeks and a small champion commitment. If it reduces ambiguity, bump to formal change." 

Templates / snippets to copy-paste:
- Slack micro-pulse (post-demo thread): "Quick pulse — what was one thing that worked well today, and one concrete next step you or the team will take before next demo? Reply with: 1) worked, 2) next step. Takes ~30–90s."
- Debrief rubric header: "Rate 0–2 on each, add comment for extremes. Tech breadth | Impact & scope | Growth signal"
- Manager invite message: "Would you be open to piloting a micro-feedback pulse in your pod for 6 weeks? Minimal lift: ask your team to reply after demos and capture 1 follow-up in your 1:1. I’ll synthesize weekly." 

Data and tracking (scratch):
- Slack channel: #leah-micro-pulse (invite only during pilot)
- Weekly capture: paste raw responses into a private sheet and mark 'actionable' vs 'not'
- Debrief variance calc: sample 12 debriefs into sheet; compute mean and sd by rubric column

Potential risks / guardrails:
- Manager fatigue: keep upstream ask minimal and optional; prepare an opt-out cadence after 3 weeks if noise high
- Feedback quality: template and examples—show "good" vs "vague" responses in kickoff
- Hiring bias: rubric must be tested for demographic impact; plan to run quick fairness snapshot before rolling beyond pilot

Open questions (need answers from manager / peers):
- Can I get two pods to pilot in July? Who are likely champions? (Priya, Marco suggested)
- Is there a preference for asynchronous Slack vs. short form in Notion? Slack lower friction but noisy
- Do we have time to run paired calibration without blocking promotion reviews? (suggest doing one per week into open calendar)

Next actions (my micro-backlog):
- [ ] Finalize Slack templates and sample responses (due 2026-03-18)
- [ ] Book 15-min sync with Priya to ask to pilot (due 2026-03-20)
- [ ] Draft rubric sheet and populate with 6 past debriefs (anonymized) by end of month
- [ ] Schedule paired calibration pilot with Samira and one eng manager (target April)
- [ ] Prepare one-slide summary for upcoming skip-level meeting

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep experiments <6 weeks to avoid momentum loss
- Avoid adding new required processes — frame as optional trial and iterate
- Capture quick wins: if any single change reduces confusion for even 1 manager, amplify

Evidence snippets (copy to manager 1:1 if asked):
- "From last week’s demo — 6/7 replies had clear 'worked' items but only 1 had a next-step. If we prompt for 'next step', we move intention into written record." (raw screenshot saved in my folder)
- "Two recent debriefs had a 1-point spread in Technical breadth across reviewers; rubric might provide shared anchor language."

Reflection (end of page):
I want experiments that are conversational and reversible. The goal is not to ship a large policy but to lower friction of clarity for ICs and reduce the noise in promotional calibration. If managers see less ambiguity, they’ll use the guidance more. Keep this page alive — update after each pilot week with short headline: participation / what changed / next-step.
